$comment: OMN-17942. The admission vocabulary for a Linear issue CREATE.
Read by plugins/onex/hooks/lib/ticket_creation_guard.py, which is invoked
by the pre_tool_use_ticket_creation_gate.sh PreToolUse hook. The vocabulary
lives here, not in the checker, so changing admission policy is a config
edit visible in one place rather than a rule a reader has to infer from a
Python literal.
JSON rather than YAML deliberately, matching agent_model_allowlist.json in
this directory: the checker sits on a fail-closed enforcement path, so it
parses its own policy with the standard library alone. A missing PyYAML in
the resolved interpreter would otherwise turn into a refusal of every
Linear write on the machine.
There is deliberately NO escape entry -- no 'any', no wildcard criterion,
no 'exempt' marker. An unbound ticket is the defect this guard refuses, and
a sanctioned spelling for it is a sanctioned incident.
prd_source -- the exact revision criterion_ids and invariant_ids were read
from. The vocabulary is sourced from a document in ANOTHER repository, so
'the ids come from the PRD' is an uncheckable claim without naming the
revision. tests/hooks/test_ticket_creation_guard.py reads the file at this
commit and at origin/main and fails on either drift, skipping with a
stated reason when no clone of that private repo is present (this repo's
CI runners do not clone it). Bump commit, criterion_ids and invariant_ids
in ONE change: a vocabulary that lags its source admits bindings to
commitments the document no longer makes, and refuses the ones it does.
criterion_ids -- the release-criterion identifiers a Gate line may cite.
C1..C27, the rows of section 6 of the beta PRD. This gate first shipped
bound to C1..C6 from beta/plans/customer-plane-validation-charter-plan.md
because the PRD then existed only on a draft PR and no C-id enumeration
was reachable at origin/main; knowledge-base-internal#125 merged to main
as cac690c3 and the enumeration now exists, so the charter is no longer a
source. INV-109 rules the customer-plane validation probes tests rather
than ship conditions, so a charter probe id is not a commitment a ticket
can bind to. No charter id had to be DROPPED: the PRD table spells
C1..C27, which covers all six charter spellings -- what changed is what
each id RESOLVES to, not whether the string is admitted.
Re-read 2026-09-13 at 91d8d837 during OMN-18331: the table had grown a
C28 row and the coverage block an INV-115 entry since the 2026-09-05
pin, so a ticket binding to either was being refused for naming a
commitment the document does make. Bumped here rather than in a separate
pass because the drift test that found it is the one gating this change,
and a red test carried forward as pre-existing is a red test nobody
owns.
invariant_ids -- the invariant identifiers a Gate line may cite. These are
the 42 entries of the PRD's machine-readable invariant-coverage block,
NOT every INV- token in the document. The PRD deliberately declines the
deploy and security scopes while citing individual invariants from them
by reference (INV-032, INV-071..INV-074, INV-086), and its section 9.2
names INV-108 as process-scoped and carried by a different document.
Binding a ticket to an id the PRD only mentions would bind it to a
commitment this document does not make, which is the defect this gate
exists to refuse.
epic_markers -- an issue with no parentId is admitted only if its
description carries one of these as a LINE OF ITS OWN, matched exactly
after trimming and lowercasing. Substring matching is refused on purpose
(omni_home CLAUDE.md rule 15): a gate that matches anywhere in the body
passes on prose that merely mentions the marker, including prose that
mentions it in order to deny it. Prefix matching is refused for a second
reason -- a line reading 'Epic: OMN-16729' NAMES a parent epic, and under
a prefix rule the ticket most tightly bound to a parent would be the one
admitted as parentless.
in_progress_state_names -- the state names/types that mean WORK IN FLIGHT.
Rule 5 fires only on a create that names one of these, matched exactly
after trimming and lowercasing against 'state', 'stateId', 'status' and
'statusType'. 'started' is Linear's state TYPE for the in-progress band,
so a create naming the type rather than the state is caught too. A raw
uuid is deliberately NOT matched: this guard has no workspace lookup and
refusing on an id it cannot resolve would make every id-shaped create
unfileable. That is the one fail-OPEN direction in this policy and it is
bounded to rule 5.
The unstarted-children cap (rule 8, OMN-18323) was RESCINDED by the operator on
2026-09-21 -- rolling work ledger RULING row 2026-09-21T14:46:45Z item (f),
"that's not something I made". Its unstarted_children_cap, unstarted_state_types
and override_ledger_* entries are gone from this policy and rule 8 is gone from
the checker. Nothing here bounds how many children a parent may carry.
residual_title_terms -- title shapes that read as work spun out of other
work rather than work bound to a commitment. Matched on word boundaries,
so 'minor' does not fire on 'minority' and 'nit' does not fire on
'monitor'. A residual belongs as a comment on its parent; the standing
rule is 'do not file follow-up tickets for residuals -- comment on the
parent'. The single exemption is a live-gate defect, because a gate
reporting green while enforcing nothing is not a residual, and burying it
in a comment thread is how it stays unfixed.
OMN-18331 (plan step 5). Rules 6 and 7 -- every acceptance criterion in a
create names the check that would settle it, and a behaviour-shaped
criterion may not name a merge-state read as that check.
falsifier_markers -- the spellings that introduce a criterion's falsifier,
matched case-insensitively INSIDE a criterion item rather than on a line
of its own. That is the one place this policy departs from the whole-line
anchoring rules 3 and 5 use, and it is deliberate: the plan's mechanism
is that the falsifier is written AS PART OF the criterion, in one act, by
the author who knows the intent. A line of its own could be appended
later, by someone else, after the outcome was known -- which is exactly
the property the mechanism exists to guarantee. The ITEM BOUNDARY does
the anchoring work instead: a falsifier belonging to the criterion above
does not discharge the one below it, which a body-wide substring rule
would let it do.
The canonical spelling is the first entry. The second is the form already
in the corpus -- OMN-18135's own criteria are written with it -- and is
admitted so the rule does not refuse tickets written the way the minting
lanes already write them.
acceptance_criteria_headings -- the heading spellings that OPEN a criteria
section, transcribed from the same parser the closer reads criteria with.
Rule 6 fires only when one of these is present. That parser falls back to
reading the WHOLE BODY when no heading is found, because there an
over-count HOLDS a flip and holding is the safe direction. Here an
over-count REFUSES a create, so the fallback is dropped on purpose. That
is a stated fail-OPEN direction bounded to rule 6: a create with no
criteria section is not gated by it, and per the plan's own failure-mode
table such a ticket simply never auto-closes -- the closer holds it on an
unbound criterion, which is today's behaviour for the entire corpus. A
degradation, not a new hole, and not a silent one.
state_criterion_markers / behaviour_criterion_markers -- transcribed from
the OMN-18135 AC4 criterion classifier named in proof_class_source.
Transcribed rather than imported because this guard is a PreToolUse hook
that parses its own policy with the standard library alone and can take
no dependency on another repository's package; the source revision is
pinned there and a test fails on drift.
THE TIE-BREAK IS INVERTED HERE, and naming that is the point. The source
asks 'may a readback discharge this criterion?' and answers yes only on a
state marker with no behaviour marker, so everything ambiguous falls to
behaviour and HOLDS a flip. This asks 'must this criterion be refused a
merge-state falsifier?' and answers yes only on a behaviour marker with
no state marker, so everything ambiguous is ADMITTED. Same wordlist,
opposite default, because the cost of being wrong is opposite: there a
misread costs a comment, here it costs a refused create, and a gate that
refuses correct work is one lanes learn to route around.
merge_state_falsifier_markers -- falsifier shapes that read MERGE STATE
rather than behaviour: the gh and git subcommands the proof-class module
classifies as merge-state, plus the prose spellings a criterion author
writes in place of a command. A falsifier matching one of these is
refused on a behaviour-shaped criterion ONLY when it names no runner from
behaviour_runner_words. That conjunction is OMN-18135's own measured
finding: the 'gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/... && <runner>' form satisfies
receipt hardening AND keeps its behaviour class, so a rule that refused
every falsifier mentioning gh would refuse the one form that clears both
gates -- and a lane that meets that refusal correctly concludes the gate
is wrong.
behaviour_runner_words -- transcribed from the proof-class module's tight
positive allowlist of test runners plus the ONEX CLI. Used here for the
single conjunction above. This policy does NOT re-implement proof
classification and must not grow toward doing so.
THE HASHING UNIT, because a later mechanism depends on it and must not
re-derive it. The plan's next step transcribes each criterion's declared
falsifier into a companion contract as an ACCEPTED binding, pinning a
criterion_hash to the criterion text as it read when the binding was
accepted, so a criterion silently rewritten afterwards no longer
satisfies it. The guard therefore EXPORTS the unit (criterion_units).
unit        -- ONE criterion item: its own bullet or AC<n> line plus any
continuation lines before the next item. Exactly the span
rule 6 reads a falsifier from, so the gate and the
transcriber cannot disagree about where one criterion
ends -- a disagreement that would bind a criterion to the
check declared for its neighbour.
canonical   -- Unicode NFC, whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces,
ends stripped, and NOTHING else. No lowercasing, no
emphasis stripping, no label removal: every further
normalisation is a rewrite the hash becomes unable to
detect. Re-wrapping is the one edit that changes the
bytes without changing what the criterion says, which is
why it is the one thing normalised.
hash        -- SHA-256 of the canonical text, UTF-8, hex. Stated as an
equation so a consumer in another repository can compute
it without importing this module.
independent -- editing one criterion leaves every other criterion's hash
byte-identical. Pinned by a test, because a shared hash
over the section would invalidate every accepted binding
on a ticket the first time an author fixed a typo.
the pair    -- the falsifier is INSIDE the hash. What an author accepts
is this criterion settled by this check, so a falsifier
swapped afterwards is as much a rewrite as a reworded
criterion; a hash over the criterion half alone would let
the check change silently under an accepted binding.
Rules 6 and 7 have no escape entry either. A criterion naming no check is
the defect they refuse, and a sanctioned spelling for it would be a
sanctioned incident.
OMN-18484. Rule 10 -- a create carries at least one criterion the closer
can bind evidence TO. Rules 6 and 7 bound what a LISTED criterion must
carry; this bounds whether there is a bindable one at all. Measured over
the 915 tickets created in the fourteen days to 2026-09-16: 64.4% carry
no labelled criterion, and 76.7% of everything In Progress carries none,
so on two tickets in three the evidence closer has nothing to key on.
min_labelled_criteria -- the fewest criteria that must carry an AC<n> or
DOD<n> ordinal. One, and one rather than all of them deliberately:
rules 6 and 7 already bound what EVERY criterion carries, and a rule
demanding a label on every one would refuse the mixed sections the
corpus is full of. The question this rule asks is whether a binding
entry has ANY label to point at -- ModelAcBinding keys on one -- and
one label answers it. A number, here, rather than a Python literal, so
an operator raises or lowers it on evidence and finds it when the
evidence changes.
This rule CLOSES the fail-OPEN stated above under
acceptance_criteria_headings. That paragraph records that rule 6
declines to fire on a description with no criteria section, because
there an over-count would refuse a create, and that such a ticket
simply never auto-closes. Never auto-closing was the whole measured
defect, so the absence is now the finding. Nothing is over-counted:
zero parsed criteria is not an ambiguous read of a section, it is the
absence of one.
labelled_criterion_exempt_binding_forms -- the binding FORM ids that
exempt a create from rule 10. One entry, parent_criterion, and the
reason it is the only one: that form spells a parent plus an
acceptance-criterion ordinal, so a create bound that way points at a
LABELLED criterion that already exists on its parent. The bindable
thing the rule demands is present -- it just lives one ticket up. Every
other declared form names a CHECK or a document id: a workflow run, a
release criterion, an invariant, a live-gate defect. None of those is a
label a binding entry can key on, so a ticket bound that way still has
to carry its own criteria. OMN-18484's own body is bound by the
workflow-run form and carries five labelled criteria, which is the
shape this rule asks for.
Form IDS rather than line spellings, and validated at load time against
gate_binding_grammar.json: an exemption naming a form the contract does
not declare can never match what the guard classifies, so it would
never fire, and a gate whose exemption never fires reads as working
while enforcing something other than what its config says.
The epic exemption is the OTHER half and is read from epic_markers
above -- an epic states a commitment and its children carry the
criteria. Both exemptions are therefore data in this file, neither is
inferred, and deleting either key refuses every create until it is
repaired rather than quietly widening what the board admits.
Stated residual, because it bounds the claim: the parent-criterion
exemption checks the SHAPE of the binding, not that the named ordinal
exists on the named parent. A create citing a parent AC that was never
written is admitted. Closing that needs a parent-body lookup on the
create path, which this guard does not have today -- it is a separate
change, not a hole this rule opened.

prd_source.invariant_ids_from: the invariant-coverage HTML-comment block in the front matter
